'''''Veronica strictissima''''', commonly known as the '''Banks Peninsula hebe''', is a [[flowering plant]] in the family [[Plantaginaceae]]. It is endemic to [[Banks Peninsula]] in [[Canterbury Region|Canterbury]], New Zealand.

==Description==
''Veronica strictissima'' grows to a rounded shrub to {{cvt|2|m}} tall.<ref name="New Zealand Plant Conservation Network">{{cite book |author=New Zealand Plant Conservation Network |url=http://www.nzpcn.org.nz/flora_details.aspx?ID=2011 |title=Veronica strictissima |date=2016}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Flora of New Zealand {{!}} Taxon Profile {{!}} Veronica strictissima |url=https://www.nzflora.info/factsheet/taxon/Veronica-strictissima.html |access-date=2025-01-21 |website=www.nzflora.info}}</ref> Its Latin name refers to its erect stems.<ref name="Chalk">{{cite book|title= Hebes and Parahebes |publisher=Timber Press |author= Chalk, D. |date= 1988}}</ref>

Leaves are opposite and narrowly oblong, {{cvt|9|–|49|mm}} long, {{cvt|3|–|8|mm}} wide.<ref name=":0" /> They are light green in colour with slightly paler undersides.<ref name=":0" />

Inflorescences are racemes up to {{cvt|17|–|107|mm}} long.<ref name=":0" /> Flowers are [[Hermaphrodite (botany)|hermaphrodite]] or female on separate plants.<ref name=":0" /> 

Capsules contain multiple tiny seeds.<ref name="Wilson">{{cite book |title=Plant life on Banks Peninsula|publisher=Manuka Press | last= Wilson | first=H. D. |authorlink=Hugh Wilson (New Zealand botanist) |date= 2013}}</ref> Seeds are flat and brown, {{cvt|1.0|–|1.6|mm|2}} long.<ref name="Bayly, Kellow">{{cite book |author=Bayly, M., & Kellow, A. |title=An Illustrated Guide to New Zealand Hebes |date=2006 |publisher=Te Papa Press}}</ref>

=== Natural global range ===
''Veronica strictissima'' is endemic to Banks Peninsula, [[Canterbury, New Zealand]].<ref name="Wilson" /><ref name="Doc 1">{{cite book|title=Native plants natural to Banks peninsula|author=Department of Conservation|date=2015|url=http://www.doc.govt.nz/Documents/conservation/native-plants/motukarara-nursery/banks-peninsula.pdf}}</ref> Multiple separate populations have been identified in the region.<ref name="Bayly, Kellow" /><ref name="Delph 1">{{cite journal |author=Delph, L. F. |date=1990 |title=Sex-ratio Variation in the Gynodiecious Shrub Hebe strictissima (Scrophulariaceae) |journal=Evolution |publisher=Evolution, 44(1), 134–142. doi:10.2307/2409529 |volume=44 |issue=1 |pages=134–142 |doi=10.2307/2409529 |jstor=2409529 |pmid=28568202}}</ref><ref name="Cockayne & Allan">{{cite book|title=The Present taxonomic status of the New Zealand Species of Hebe |publisher=Transactions of the New Zealand Institute | author1-link=Leonard Cockayne | last1= Cockayne | first1=L. | last2=Allan |first2=H. H. |author2-link=Harry Allan |url=http://rsnz.natlib.govt.nz/volume/rsnz_57/rsnz_57_00_000140.pdf |date= 1925}}</ref><ref name="Te Papa">{{cite book|title=Object: Veronica Strictissima (Kirk) Garn.-Jones; lectotype of Veronica parviflora var. strictissima Kirk |url=http://collections.tepapa.govt.nz/Object/261111 |author= Museum of New Zealand Te Papa|date= 1876}}</ref>

=== Habitat preferences ===
''Veronica'' ''strictissima'' is an [[Ruderal species|early coloniser]] of disturbed habitats, occurring in sunny, open areas, such as rocky outcrops, cliffs,<ref name="Wilson" /> scrubland,<ref name="Bayly, Kellow" /> and roadside banks from sea level up to {{cvt|853|m|-2}}.<ref name="Wilson" />

Banks Peninsula differs in soil composition compared to other areas of Canterbury, it is made up of [[loess]] and [[basalt]] rock, while lower Canterbury is predominantly [[Alluvium|alluvial]].<ref name="Griffiths.">{{cite journal |author=Griffiths, E |date=1973 |title=Loess of Banks peninsula |journal=New Zealand Journal of Geology and Geophysics |publisher=New Zealand Journal of Geology and Geophysics, 16(3), 657–675. doi:10.1080/00288306.1973.10431388 |volume=16 |issue=3 |pages=657–675 |bibcode=1973NZJGG..16..657G |doi=10.1080/00288306.1973.10431388 |doi-access=free}}</ref> ''V. strictissima'' has been found to prefer moderate levels of moisture with low salinity and good soil drainage.<ref name="Nature services" />

==Phenology==
''Veronica strictissima'' flowers in summer, sometimes till early autumn.<ref name=":0" /><ref name="Bayly, Kellow" />  Individual plants will flower for 2–5 weeks.<ref name="Delph 1" /> The flowers on the spike of one plant will normally flower simultaneously.<ref name="Delph 1" /> Flowers are pollinated by a single species of bee native to New Zealand, ''[[Lasioglossum sordidum]].''<ref name="Delph 1" /> Seed capsules form during autumn<ref name="Bayly, Kellow"/> before dehiscing in late autumn.<ref name="Delph 1"/> Seeds are wind dispersed,<ref name="Doc 2">{{cite book |author=Department of Conservation |url=http://www.doc.govt.nz/get-involved/run-a-project/restoration-advice/native-plant-restoration/ecosource-seeds/collection-and-propagation-guide-trees/ |title=Seed collection and propagation guide for native trees and shrubs |date=n.d.}}</ref><ref name="Thornson, Dickson & Seddon">{{cite book|title=Flora of New Zealand. Volume 1.Seed dispersal systems in the New Zealand flora |publisher=file:///C:/Users/David%20beukes/Downloads/1-s2.0-S1433831909000237-main.pdf |author= Thornsen, M. J., Dickson, K. J. M., & Seddon|date= 2009}}</ref> but can also be dispersed by birds and lizards.<ref name="Nature services">{{cite book|title=Hebe Strictissima|url=http://natureservices.landcareresearch.co.nz/app/plant/459|author-link=Harry Allan|last=Allan|first=H.|date=n.d.}}{{Dead link|date=April 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> 

==Ecology==
''Veronica strictissima'' is grazed upon by sheep, goats and cows.<ref name="Wilson"/><ref name="Delph 1" /> The nectar and fruit are eaten by lizards and birds.<ref name= "Nature services"/> ''V. strictissima'' and other species from the genus ''Veronica'' are fed on by [[Platyptilia]], ''[[Xyridacma veronicae]]''.<ref name="Crowe">{{cite book|title=Which Native Forest Plant?|publisher=Penguin Books (NZ) LTD: Penguin |author=Crow, A. |date= 2009}}</ref>

==Cultural uses==
''Veronica strictissima'' was used as a cure for [[dysentery]] during [[World War II]].<ref name="Crowe" /> [[Māori people|Māori]] used the plant as a traditional medicine for the treatment of ulcers, headaches, kidney and bladder troubles.<ref name= "Crowe"/>

==Other information==
''Veronica strictissima'' can be confused with other ''Veronica'' species, and was once included with ''[[Veronica leiophylla]]''<ref name= "Chalk"/> and ''[[Veronica parviflora]].''<ref name="Cockayne & Allan" /> It is very similar to ''[[Veronica traversii]]'', which is far more widespread throughout New Zealand, being found in the [[Marlborough District|Marlborough]] and [[Nelson, New Zealand|Nelson]] districts as well as Canterbury.<ref name="Wilson"/>

''Veronica strictissima'' may hybridise with ''[[Veronica salicifolia]].''<ref name=":0" />
